issue.title: Stale job lock prevents worker from draining pending queue after network partition

summary.problem: Worker processes stop accepting jobs after reconnecting following a momentary Redis network disconnect.
summary.rootCause: The heartbeat lock lease timestamp is not reset on reconnect, causing stale lock checks to block queue polling.
summary.patchTarget: src/engine/worker.py: reset lock lease expiry in handle_reconnect() before resuming poll loop.

trail.title: Redis client disconnect hook
trail.description: Receives reconnection event from underlying redis transport.

explanation.simple: When connection returns, the worker re-registers its poll task.
explanation.detailed: on_transport_reconnect callback fires and triggers resume_poll_loop(), but fails to invalidate current lock cache.
explanation.deep: Introduced in v0.9 to prevent worker stampedes on reconnect, but assumed local lock lease was already purged.

code.lines:
def on_transport_reconnect(self):
    logger.info("Transport reconnected; resuming worker tasks")
    self._is_connected = True
    self.resume_poll_loop()
code.pointer: Does not clear self._active_lease_id or update last_heartbeat

trail.title: Queue poll iteration
trail.description: Main job scheduling tick checking for available work.

explanation.simple: Worker checks if it has permission to poll by inspecting its lease.
explanation.detailed: poll_next_job() calls ensure_worker_lock() before querying the queue.
explanation.deep: Lock gating ensures only one designated leader worker handles delayed queues.

trail.title: Lock lease validity check
trail.description: Checks if existing lease is expired according to local monotonic clock.

explanation.simple: The lock manager compares current timestamp with the cached heartbeat from before disconnect.
explanation.detailed: is_lease_valid() detects time delta exceeds threshold, but rejects acquisition without issuing an explicit release command.
explanation.deep: A stale local lease prevents new lock acquisition until remote TTL expires in Redis (default 60s), leaving worker idle.

code.pointer: Returns False but retains stale lease_id reference

trail.title: Reconnect lease invalidation & reset
trail.description: Where lease invalidation and immediate renewal must be wired.

explanation.simple: Reset local lock cache upon transport recovery before resuming queue poll loop.
explanation.detailed: Call lock_manager.reset_local_state() in handle_reconnect to force fresh lock election immediately.
explanation.deep: Ensures no lingering timestamps from before the network blip block worker activation.

code.pointer: Clear local cache so fresh acquisition occurs on next tick

interactions.error: StaleLeaseError: cached lease held but expired

mustKeepTrue: Workers must never dual-execute the same delayed task concurrently.
Redis TTL expiry mechanism must remain unchanged as safe fallback.
Clean shutdowns must continue releasing lock leases explicitly.
permittedToChange: Local in-memory lease cache invalidation rules on transport reconnect.
Immediate lock re-election trigger on reconnect event.
suggestedTestCases: Simulate 5s network silence, restore transport, and assert job accepted within 100ms.
checklist: Verify reset_local_state() cleans up all active lease keys
Confirm no race condition between reconnect event and active poll thread
Verify backwards compatibility with standalone non-clustered Redis

glossary.Lease: A time-bounded exclusive token allowing a worker to poll queues.
glossary.Partition: A temporary network disconnection separating workers from storage.
glossary.Poll Tick: The periodic polling interval where workers check for pending tasks.

contextNotes.text: Do not test on live production queues without setting a mock queue prefix.
Nova engine uses leader election per queue partition to prevent task duplicate execution.

maintainerQuestions: Should reconnect immediately trigger an active election or wait for next scheduled poll tick?
Is 60s the intended remote TTL for all queue worker types or just priority queues?

adversarialChallenges.challenge: Does line 84 execute if the socket connection is already closed?
adversarialChallenges.counterHypothesis: Early return in event loop might bypass token expiration logic.
adversarialChallenges.resolution: Refuted: Stop 2 line 52 verifies that the socket listener remains active until a disconnect event is emitted.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: Could Redis server clock skew explain the 60s lease timeout instead of local worker state retention?
adversarialChallenges.counterHypothesis: Clock synchronization lag between worker nodes and Redis master node.
adversarialChallenges.resolution: Refuted: Stop 2 lines 80-84 show worker caching lease expiry in local memory rather than reading remote TTL.
